title: Persist worker credential hashes across Lambda instances
description:
**Found on live development ThinTurn after named deploy of #142.**

`POST /orgs/{tenant}/workers/register` returns 200. Claim/chunks work. Full `live_aws_thin_turn.sh development` then fails:

stale_waiting 403 invalid worker credential

Expected 409 on the duplicate /waiting after the SSE stream. The first /waiting on the same bearer succeeds.

ControlPlane._workers holds token_hash in process memory only. A later Lambda instance does not see the registration.

**Do:** persist worker records (including SHA-256 token hash) in the same store as other control-plane rows so verify survives recycle. Gherkin first. One path. Do not add a second auth bypass.

**Done when:** `cd python && sh scripts/live_aws_thin_turn.sh development` exits 0 against development after a named ChatticusThinTurn deploy. Computers desiredCount 0. Never `--all`.

comments.text: Planning in `/tmp/chatticus-b3e12c-worker-hash` branch `cursor/worker-hash-persist-b3e12c-4a21`. Unblocks a green live thin-turn for d71ed5. Computers desiredCount 0. Never `--all`.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
**Correct diagnosis, and this is not a new failure mode. It is the fifth instance of one this repository has already fixed four times.**

Worker state is not in the store at all. `messaging/store.py` has no worker methods, and `register_worker` in `control_plane.py` holds registrations in process, so every Lambda instance has its own view and a worker registered against one instance is unauthenticated against the next. The symptom is a 401 on a valid token, which reads as an authentication bug and is a persistence bug.

Phase 1 closed four stories that are this exact defect for other entities:

- 206992, read a channel's active turn after Front Door recycle
- 28503e, durable bot name uniqueness survives Front Door recycle
- 2b4fc0, list a user's active turns after Front Door recycle
- 3a94d6, bot memory writes hydrate from the store after Front Door recycle

Worker registration is the one entity that never got that treatment, because until credentials arrived nothing depended on it surviving a recycle. Those four are the template; follow whichever is closest rather than inventing a fifth shape.

**Concrete fix shape.** Bots and computers already live under `_roster_pk(tenant_id)` with a per-entity sort key. A worker record belongs in the same partition, sort key `worker#{worker_id}`, carrying the token hash, cost class, and capabilities. That keeps a tenant's workers in the partition that is already the tenant's roster and needs no new access pattern.

**Worth a scenario, not just a fix:** a worker registers, the front door recycles, and the same credential still authenticates. That is the shape all four prior stories used, and it is what stops this returning a sixth time.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
**Reviewed #147. The persistence fix is right. The heartbeat it introduced needs a second look.**

The fix follows the four prior recycle stories precisely: `put_worker`, `get_worker`, and `list_workers` on both store implementations, keyed on `_roster_pk(tenant_id)` with a `worker#` sort prefix, so workers sit in the same partition as bots and computers with no new access pattern. The Gherkin scenario is the same shape those stories used, and it is backed by two tests, one for the in-memory store and one against DynamoDB. The extra scenario for the same `worker_id` registering on two tenants was not asked for and is the right instinct.

**The concern: heartbeat now writes to DynamoDB, and writes nothing new.**

```python
def heartbeat(self, tenant_id: str, worker_id: str) -> None:
    record = self.worker(tenant_id, worker_id)
    self._messaging_store.put_worker(record)
```

A read followed by a write of the same unmutated record. Two things follow.

- **The write carries no information.** If the point is liveness, the record needs a `last_seen` that the write updates, and nothing currently reads liveness anyway. As written it is a round trip that changes no bytes, so either a timestamp is missing or the write is.
- **It is an idle floor.** Registered workers heartbeat while idle, so this is a steady read-and-write pair per worker that continues while nobody is working. `AGENTS.md` and `docs/STACK.md` put that squarely against the premise: serverless here is about the idle floor, and nothing should bill while nobody is working. At one household it is pennies; it grows with every worker in every deployment, and it grows while those deployments are asleep.

Deciding what heartbeat is for settles both. If liveness matters, add the timestamp and give something a reason to read it. If it does not, drop the write and let registration be the only durable moment.

**Optional, not required.** `verify_worker_token` iterates every worker in the tenant because a bare bearer token cannot name its own worker. Shaping the credential as `worker_id` plus secret would make verification a point read instead. I am not asking for it on load grounds, since the non-requirements are explicit that this workload has none, but it would take a scan off the authentication path for free the next time that code is touched.

CI was still running when I looked, so this is a review note rather than a merge signal.
